title: Fallen Heroes Flag Act of 2016
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate passed version is repeated here.)

Fallen Heroes Flag Act of 2016

(Sec. 3) This bill allows the Representative or Senator of an immediate family member of a deceased firefighter, law enforcement officer, member of a rescue squad or ambulance crew, or public safety officer who died in the line of duty to give the family, on request, a Capitol-flown flag, together with a certificate, signed by the official providing the flag (the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the Representative, or the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Senator), that contains an expression of sympathy for the family.

summary.headline: A 2016 law lets a member of Congress give the family of a fallen first responder a flag flown over the Capitol, with a sympathy certificate.
summary.what_it_does: The law lets the Representative or Senator of an immediate family member of a deceased firefighter, police officer, rescue or ambulance crew member, or other public safety officer killed in the line of duty request a Capitol-flown flag for the family. The flag comes with a signed certificate that expresses sympathy. The Speaker of the House or the President pro tempore of the Senate signs it, along with the sponsoring member.
summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary gives no separate start date, so the law took effect on its enactment date, May 16, 2016.
